title: Avengers: Doomsday essential watchlist: a complete 20-day Marvel marathon
excerpt: A daily viewing calendar covering the original X-Men, both seasons of Loki and key MCU films before Avengers: Doomsday.
seo_description: Follow a complete 20-day Marvel viewing schedule with key X-Men movies, Loki episodes and MCU films before December 18, 2026.
body_md:
With Avengers: Doomsday scheduled for December 18, 2026, a full Marvel rewatch might seem impossible. Fortunately, viewers do not need to revisit every theatrical release or television series to refresh the most relevant storylines. Disney and Marvel previously shared an essential viewing selection at San Diego Comic-Con. It brings together older X-Men adventures, important Avengers chapters, multiverse stories and newer superhero teams.

The following calendar starts on November 27 and finishes on December 16. Most days require one movie, while the Loki portion calls for two episodes per day.

## Your daily Marvel viewing calendar

- November 27 — X-Men (2000): revisit the original cinematic introductions of several familiar mutants.
- November 28 — X2 (2003): explore the team's relationships and the arrival of Nightcrawler.
- November 29 — Captain America: The First Avenger: refresh Steve Rogers' origin.
- November 30 — The Avengers: see Earth's heroes assemble.
- December 1 — Avengers: Infinity War: revisit the confrontation with Thanos.
- December 2 — Avengers: Endgame: review the consequences of defeat and time travel.
- December 3 — Loki, season 1, episodes 1–2: meet the Time Variance Authority.
- December 4 — Loki, season 1, episodes 3–4: explore variants.
- December 5 — Loki, season 1, episodes 5–6: understand the Void and its inhabitants.
- December 6 — Loki, season 2, episodes 1–2: return to the troubled TVA.
- December 7 — Loki, season 2, episodes 3–4: examine the growing temporal crisis.
- December 8 — Loki, season 2, episodes 5–6: complete Loki's journey.
- December 9 — Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: meet Shang-Chi.
- December 10 — Spider-Man: No Way Home: revisit a crossover between cinematic worlds.
- December 11 — Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: understand incursions.
- December 12 — Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: revisit Wakanda and Namor.
- December 13 — Captain America: Brave New World: catch up with Sam Wilson.
- December 14 — Deadpool & Wolverine: return to variants and the TVA.
- December 15 — Thunderbolts*: meet the newly assembled team.
- December 16 — The Fantastic Four: First Steps: get acquainted with Marvel's first family.

## What the marathon accomplishes

The schedule balances character history with the rules of the multiverse. Starting outside the MCU makes sense because the crossover draws on a much broader screen history than the Avengers movies alone. Loki provides particularly useful context for understanding alternate timelines, although the exact role these concepts will play in Doomsday remains uncertain.

Finishing on December 16 leaves December 17 available for rest or early screenings. Treat the list as a helpful refresher rather than an admission requirement: the upcoming film's precise narrative connections have yet to be established.
